userStories.title: Report story-review verdict mismatches and retry once
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Replace synthetic story findings with explicit mismatch facts and spend the existing reviewer retry on a concrete follow-up.

**Motivation** — The implementer then gets a fix round with nothing concrete to fix.

**Approach** — **Verdict mismatch (#2921).** `parseStoryReviewReply` stops adding synthetic findings. `StoryReviewVerdict` gains an optional field:
```ts
export type VerdictMismatch = "spec" | "quality";
// on StoryReviewVerdict:
readonly mismatch?: readonly VerdictMismatch[];
```
`"spec"` is listed when `spec` is `"fail"` and no finding has `kind: "spec"` with a severity other than `minor`. `"quality"` is listed when `quality` is `"changes"` and no finding of any kind has a severity other than `minor`. The order is `spec` then `quality`. The key is absent when neither holds.

Branch review keeps today's behaviour. `parseBranchReviewReply` applies the two floors itself after calling `parseStoryReviewReply`, in today's order and with the same texts: the spec floor first, then the quality floor only when no finding with a severity other than `minor` remains after the spec floor. A reply with `spec: "fail"`, `quality: "changes"` and no findings therefore still gets one synthetic finding, the spec one. It returns no `mismatch` key.

`workflowStoryReviewOp` (`packages/nax/src/operations/workflow-story-review.ts`) uses its one existing retry for the follow-up. Its retry `validate` rejects a parsed verdict that carries `mismatch`. Its `prompts.invalid` receives the last output: when that output parses to a verdict with `mismatch` it returns `buildWorkflowVerdictMismatchRetry(mismatch)`, otherwise `buildWorkflowReviewJsonRetry()` as today. `maxAttempts` stays 2 and `exhaustedFallback` is unchanged. Once the retry is spent, the op's own `parse` of the last reply is the result: a verdict that still carries `mismatch`, or `null` when the last reply does not parse. A reply that was first unparseable and then mismatched gets no third turn.

`buildWorkflowVerdictMismatchRetry` is a new function in `packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-story-review-builder.ts`, exported from `@/prompts`:
```ts
export function buildWorkflowVerdictMismatchRetry(mismatch: readonly VerdictMismatch[]): string;
```
For `"spec"` it says: `You returned spec: fail but no critical or important spec finding. Either name the acceptance criterion that fails as a finding, or change the verdict to pass.` For `"quality"` it says: `You returned quality: changes but no critical or important finding. Either name the defect as a finding, or change the verdict to approved.` It ends with the same reply-shape instruction `buildWorkflowReviewJsonRetry` gives.

**Scope** — In: parser/type/barrel changes, exact branch floors, retry prompt and callOp integration tests. Out: US-003 loop recording and model summaries; US-007 minor promotion and branch-fix priority. The re-review verdict shape and parser are unchanged. Branch review gets no follow-up turn.

**Interface** — `parseStoryReviewReply(output: string): StoryReviewVerdict | null` and `parseBranchReviewReply(output: string, minorIds: readonly string[]): BranchReviewVerdict | null` keep their signatures; the new union/optional field and builder signature above are the target contracts.

The reviewer's follow-up reply is unparseable: the op returns `null`, the review is skipped as today (`unparseable reply`) and the story closes unreviewed. The reviewer's follow-up reply still carries a mismatch: the verdict is used with its findings; ledgering/recording is US-003. Keep the final parser permissive even though retry validation is stricter. Use the existing parse-retry seam; do not change the shared retry budget/dispatcher. Revise the three existing synthetic story-finding tests in test/unit/operations/workflow-replies.test.ts to assert no added finding and mismatch, and prove the same inputs still receive branch floors. New integration tests must enter through callOp(ctx, workflowStoryReviewOp, input) with scripted replies, asserting exact turn count, prompt and final result.

userStories.title: Promote deferred defects and fix blocking branch findings first
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let branch review promote deferred minors into blocking findings and prioritize blocking work before fix-now minors.

**Motivation** — Some were real defects filed too low, and a branch-fix session that hit its step limit had no order to work in.

**Approach** — **Minors triage (#2920).** `MinorTriageDecision` becomes `"promote" | "fix-now" | "leave"`. The branch review prompt (`packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-branch-builder.ts`) states the three by consequence:

`Triage each deferred minor: "promote" when it describes wrong behaviour a user or caller can reach (it is then fixed as a blocking finding), "fix-now" when it is a real defect or a breach of a project rule worth fixing before the PR, or "leave" when it is style, comment wording, formatting or duplication that no project rule names (it is listed in the PR body and not fixed). Its "minorTriage" entry is its whole verdict: do not repeat a deferred minor as a finding.`

The reply shape reads `"decision": "promote|fix-now|leave"`. `parseBranchReviewReply` accepts `promote`; an unknown or missing decision still reads as `leave`.

`branchReviewStep` (`packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-steps.ts`) turns each promoted minor into a blocking finding `{ kind: "quality", severity: "important", issue: "<storyId>: <text>" }`, assigned a B id after the reviewer's own blocking findings. The minor stays in the record with `triage: "promote"`, so it is in neither the fix-now group nor the PR body's left-minors list. The branch quality floor (`withQualityFloor`) adds its synthetic finding only when the verdict has no blocking finding of its own and no minor was promoted: a promoted minor is the concrete item to fix. The step line adds the promoted count only when it is above zero: `deferred minors: 2 promote, 3 fix-now, 9 leave`, and `deferred minors: 3 fix-now, 9 leave` when none was promoted.

`branchFixStep` orders round 1's items as review findings, then gate findings, then fix-now minors. `buildWorkflowBranchFixPrompt` renders findings with a severity other than `minor` under `## Findings to fix` and the minor ones under a second heading `## Minor findings to fix after those`, which is omitted when there is none. The "How to work" list gains `Fix the findings in the first list before the minor ones.`

The run summary's `branch` view gains `minors: { found, promoted, fixNow, left }`, counted from the record's `minors` list by triage (`left` is the `leave` count) and present only when that list is not empty. The existing `minorsLeft` keeps its meaning: the `leave` count plus the record's `newMinors`. `formatWorkflowSummary` prints `Deferred minors: 9 found, 2 promoted, 3 fix-now, 4 left`.

**Scope** — In: shared triage union/parser, exact consequence prompt/reply shape, promotion and B IDs, step-level quality-floor guard, first-round branch-fix order and prompt partition, optional summary counts. Out: US-002 story parser/retry changes and relocation of branch parser floors; US-003 story mismatch metrics. Deferred minors triaged `leave` are not removed from the PR body, and the story reviewer's own severity wording (changed by #2922) is not edited again. Branch review gets no mismatch follow-up.

**Interface**
```typescript
export type MinorTriageDecision = "promote" | "fix-now" | "leave";
// WorkflowSummaryView.branch gains:
minors?: { found: number; promoted: number; fixNow: number; left: number };
```

analysis:
Repository exploration and architecture: This is an enhancement of @nathapp/nax, not greenfield. All nine implementation stories are scoped to packages/nax and retain the spec's binding dependencies. The codebase-memory MCP server is unavailable in this tool set, so discovery used direct Read, Glob and Grep. No implementation or validation commands were run while drafting. The requested PRD is a planning artifact; no implementation story may author a file under .nax/. Read docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:19 for dependency injection, :26 for concurrency/testing, and :156 for hard limits: 600 source lines and 800 test lines. Use Bun-native APIs, strict TypeScript, existing barrel exports and _deps seams; do not introduce direct nax-ai imports, alter permissions, or change agent/session infrastructure. The feature fixes five sources of wasted work found across 34 runs (110.6 h), approximately 15 h total; the concurrency optimization remains opt-in. Pipeline mode is untouched (the current architecture documentation also describes workflow as the sole effective execution mode; do not revive or modify legacy mode behavior).

Story loop and shared integration: packages/nax/src/workflow/story-loop.ts:37 declares the injected steps, :114 the environment, :145 the in-memory graph state and :188 runStoryLoop. packages/nax/src/workflow/story-steps.ts:311 currently absorbs the first review, :386 evaluates gates -> suite -> report -> review, :469 evaluates early-stop routing, :514 runs residual adjudication and :568 closes. This file is exactly 576 lines and has little headroom under 600. Put mismatch recording in new verdict-mismatch.ts (US-003), timeout policy and routing helpers in new timeout-stop.ts (US-004/005/006), and parallel settlement/measurement in new suite-review-pass.ts (US-009); leave thin calls in story-steps.ts rather than growing it past the limit. Existing helpers and phases must retain their semantics. packages/nax/src/workflow/story-graph.ts:32 lists evaluate's declared outputs, and :55 lists residual's; graph patches must agree with produces. Add timeoutAsked to the initial state and evaluate output in US-005. If residual changes suiteThisIteration to track that it actually ran a suite, declare that output too. Track current and previous suite provenance separately: evaluate resets suiteThisIteration and returns immediately on red ordinary gates while retaining a suite object from an older pass. That old object's timedOut must never trigger timeout routing or gateTimeouts for a new pass. Preserve existing cost-stop precedence, no-work guards, pending-session findings, report allowance, finding IDs, re-review fix-base retention and residual rulings. A config-induced retry is another gate pass in the same evaluate node, not another implementer round.

US-001 analysis: packages/nax/src/test-runners/scoped-selection.ts:91 owns selection; its fullSuite helper at :97 uses fallbackFullSuiteCommand and flags, while its scoped helper at :105 always declares isFullSuite false today. Compare QualityCommandSpec structurally and exactly: a string matches the same string; arrays match only arrays with the same strings in order. No trimming, shell normalization, command equivalence inference, or orchestrator-based coverage inference. Compare the built command against input.testCommand, then use fullSuite() without options when equal. packages/nax/src/operations/verify-scoped.ts:45/:55 define output/deps and :115 the operation. Its deferred skip requires !thresholdFallback and !isMonorepoOrchestrator; retain those conditions. The zero-test fallback around :294 changes effectiveCommand and isFullSuite after selection, so coversFullSuite must reflect the final executed command, not only the initial selection. Only passed + isFullSuite + exact full-suite resolver command equality yields true; every skip, failure and timeout returns false. Resolve against ctx.packageView.config with input.workdir and input.packagePrefix, not a root-only slice or the absolute directory as a package key. packages/nax/src/quality/command-resolver.ts:71 resolves review.commands.test precedence, package placeholders and orchestrator promotion. packages/nax/src/operations/full-suite-gate.ts:143 already consumes that resolver from the package-merged config. Missing/throwing resolution must fail safe to false without changing the successful scoped result. Do not add a second resolver policy or reuse by parsed pass count. packages/nax/src/workflow/gates.ts:83 combines gates and :116 runs them; propagate suiteCovered only when true. In evaluate synthesize the specified green suite result, set suiteThisIteration and emit the exact reuse ledger line so residual cannot repeat the suite. Required literal fixture migrations: test/unit/workflow/gates.test.ts:40 green gets coversFullSuite:false (existing assertions unchanged); fakeDeps in test/unit/operations/verify-scoped.test.ts and verify-scoped-scratch.test.ts gets resolveFullSuiteCommand resolving undefined. Existing selectScopedTests unit tests live at test/unit/test-runners/scoped-selection.test.ts:21. Operations and workflow gates import VerifyScopedOutput through src/operations/index.ts:75, so keep barrel types synchronized. This is a required internal type addition, not a persisted-result migration.

US-002/003 analysis: packages/nax/src/operations/workflow-types.ts:42 defines StoryReviewVerdict and :81 BranchReviewVerdict extends it; the dependency direction is operations -> consumed by workflow, never import workflow back into operations. packages/nax/src/operations/workflow-replies.ts:129 currently appends SPEC_FAIL_ISSUE then QUALITY_CHANGES_ISSUE and :189 branches by delegating to that parser. Remove floors only from the story parser, compute optional mismatch from sanitized original findings in spec/quality order, and reapply the exact existing texts and order inside the branch parser, removing mismatch from its returned shape. A dual fail/changes empty reply gets one spec floor in branch review, not two findings. The out-of-scope prose saying branch keeps both synthetic findings means preserve both floor rules; explicit US-002 AC12 determines the single-finding result. Existing story synthetic tests at test/unit/operations/workflow-replies.test.ts:122, :130 and :141 must be revised and paired with branch regression assertions. packages/nax/src/operations/workflow-story-review.ts:44 configures one retry (maxAttempts:2), :43 supplies the lenient final parse. packages/nax/src/agents/retry/parse-retry.ts:10 exposes invalid(lastOutput), and :67 reserves truncation prompts for unparseable output. Reject mismatch only in retry validation, not in the operation's final parser. packages/nax/src/operations/call-dispatch-run.ts:274 probes retry validity per turn and :464/:473 performs the final typed parse, explaining why an exhausted mismatch must still return a verdict despite exhaustedFallback:null. Exercise this through callOp with a scripted agent, not just by inspecting retry configuration; do not modify shared dispatch to force null on a parseable mismatch. An unparseable then mismatched reply still has exactly two turns. Add buildWorkflowVerdictMismatchRetry to the builder and src/prompts/index.ts:146 export block; export VerdictMismatch through src/operations/index.ts:98 and workflow/types.ts:2 where consumed. Keep prompt dependency boundaries: the story builder currently declares a structural gate-state type locally at :11, so import the new type from its owning operations type module or another permitted type-only route rather than a runtime workflow dependency. packages/nax/src/workflow/story-steps.ts:326 already filters by severity, so mismatch recording must not create findings or convert verdict labels into blocking work. Continue ledgerCannotVerify, minor deferral, assigning IDs and fixing real blocking findings even on mismatch. Persist the optional model from StepModel.model, not agentName. Count one mismatched story record per model, not one count per mismatch kind. Sort model rows, use unknown for absent model and omit the summary key if none. New module tests must also enter runStoryLoop so the producer-consumer seam is proven.

US-004/005/006 analysis: packages/nax/src/workflow/gates.ts:149 treats passed-on-timeout as red and preserves a specific timeout finding; add timeout facts without changing these states/findings. Its guarded wrapper :65 turns non-abort errors into ordinary red findings, not timeout markers. Read explicit status, never infer timeout by finding text. packages/nax/src/workflow/blocked-stop.ts:54 is the existing ledger-owning early stop; new gateTimeoutRoute must be pure and compare explicit timedOut sets across current and immediately previous passes, with baseline taking precedence. Return all current timed-out gates if any repeat, not just the intersection. packages/nax/src/verification/test-baseline.ts:56 defines the timeout sentinel and :109 reads it; baseline capture and files remain untouched. packages/nax/src/quality/gate-timeout.ts:26 is the limit SSOT. packages/nax/src/workflow/stage-env.ts:58 builds the env; :148 wires gates and suite through closures over mutable current, :152 wires storyReview, and configChangeSteps at :274 can reload that context. Wire timeoutFacts with injected external reads and the existing resolver, reading the feature's run-start baseline. Read timeoutFacts only on a pass with current timeout evidence; unwired/throwing means healthy/unknown baseline and no limitSeconds, warn on a throw. The first healthy-baseline timeout still gets one fix round. Routing precedes and replaces stopOnUnchangedBlock only when fired, irrespective of DONE_WITH_CONCERNS/BLOCKED. timeoutAsked is a per-story loop allowance independent of implementer question count; initialize false, persist through evaluate patches, and never ask again after applying a change and retrying.

Advisor path: packages/nax/src/workflow/advisor.ts:30 is ImplementerQuestionRequest and :48 WorkflowAdvisor; extend the question status union, not ImplementerStatus. Add GateTimeoutFacts and timing to this request. Only scoped timeout can gather configFacts([scoped]); a full-suite-only timeout must omit facts and make no configFacts call. packages/nax/src/workflow/advisor-live.ts:112 currently constructs a generic implementer draft; add the exact timeout summary and gate evidence first, retaining buildMenu and its approved answer/hold/config-change candidates. A timeout string answer is advice to ledger, never an answer turn to an implementer. Catch injected answerQuestion throws, warn, then cap. packages/nax/src/workflow/config-change-absorb.ts:113 applies and records config changes; reuse it, including its refusal ledger and rollback-failure propagation, rather than copying transactions or writing config in a new helper. Its :145 changeOutcome downgrades normal write throws to write-failed but deliberately rethrows failed rollback; do not swallow that exceptional existing containment behavior. An applied change re-evaluates without spending a fix turn; no change, a refusal/write failure or a second routed timeout exits capped to residual. close.ts:9 derives terminal state: cost limit still wins; name timeout only if every red gate is among timedOut. US-006 passes only last-pass/residual-run timeout facts into close and optionally records gateTimeouts. Retained older suite states must not contribute timeout markers. Existing test/unit/workflow/story-graph.test.ts EXPECTED_PRODUCES.evaluate must add timeoutAsked in US-005. Existing blocked-stop/config-change/no-op/residual tests provide regression coverage; new entrypoint tests must prove actual step/advisor calls, warning fallbacks, repeat prevention and no stale-suite route. New buildStoryEnv timeoutFacts integration tests can use temporary baseline artifacts; never edit this repository's .nax/ files.

US-007 analysis: packages/nax/src/operations/workflow-types.ts:77 and workflow/types.ts:203 share MinorTriageDecision across records, so extend the single union. workflow-replies.ts:178 triageOf accepts only two values today and branch parsing maps missing/unknown to leave. Keep known-id ordering and fallback. packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/workflow-branch-builder.ts:132 pins reply JSON and :177 contains old cheap triage wording; replace those with the specified three-consequence wording, leaving the story reviewer's severity wording untouched. packages/nax/src/workflow/feature-steps.ts:122 has a separate withQualityFloor, :128 branchReviewStep assigns B IDs after triaging, and :178 branchFixStep currently orders review, minors, gates. Allocate promoted concrete quality/important drafts after the reviewer's own blocking drafts, preserve triage:promote in the minor record, and do not include promoted minors in either fixNowMinors or left-minors. Update only the step-level quality floor for promoted concrete work; retain the branch parser floors required by US-002, rather than silently changing branch parser policy. feature-steps.ts also has restated-minor filtering and artifact writing; preserve that behavior and avoid duplicating a promoted item as both M and B. Round 1 input must be review -> gates -> fix-now minors; follow-up target selection is unchanged. Branch builder :230 renders fix input; partition by severity and omit the minor heading when empty. run-summary.ts:35 already computes minorsLeft as leave+newMinors, :40 counts B IDs excluding gate IDs; preserve those meanings while adding triage counts only for nonempty minors. Known fixture changes: workflow-branch-builder.test.ts reply shape and feature-machine.test.ts IDs [B3,B1,B2,M1]. Leave-minor PR publishing paths stay unchanged and must continue excluding promote via the existing leave predicate.

US-008/009 analysis: packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types-workflow.ts:81 has an optional review block with coverageRetries; schemas-workflow.ts:16 parses review using prefault and :23 derives WORKFLOW_REVIEW_DEFAULTS. Add a default-false boolean to that same schema/type, not a second defaults constant. Update cli/config-descriptions.ts:106 parent description and add a child description including the gitignored-output warning. buildStoryEnv must use (workflow.review ?? WORKFLOW_REVIEW_DEFAULTS).parallelWithSuite === true for sparse hand-built configs and forward the new third storyReview argument to runStoryReview's fourth parameter. story-review.ts:97 builds the review prompt and underReviewLimit at :21 returns ran:false for ordinary timeout/unparseable output but rethrows abort. Builder :17 constructs the gates line; when suiteRunning, do not fabricate a full-suite state and explicitly tell the reviewer not to list the running suite in cannotVerify. Existing equality anchors: schemas-workflow-review.test.ts:7/:11/:26, workflow-config.test.ts default object, and removed-config-keys.test.ts project-loading review object; preserve coverageRetries and continued removal of sliceFiles. US-008 is configuration/prompt plumbing only; actual overlap is US-009.

Concurrency constraints: US-009 alone changes scheduling, and only with parallelReview true, resume null, first review not yet attempted, green ordinary gates and no suiteCovered. In that path runReportCheck before either async task; sequential path keeps suite-before-report behavior and red suite bypass of re-review before the cap. Await both to settlement, with rejection handlers attached promptly so the first failure cannot cause an unhandled rejection while waiting for the other; rethrow after the other settles, never orphan gate processes. Record elapsed times using exactly three env.now/Date.now reads: start and one per settled task; overlap is min(elapsed suite,elapsed review), not wall time, task sum or role timing sum. Absorb review findings/minors/mismatch/cannotVerify and skipped-review state as usual, and combine suite and review findings even if suite is red before the cap. Cached suiteCovered must remain sequential and render full-suite green. Re-reviews and any resumed story remain sequential. packages/nax/src/review/reviewer-guard/guard.ts:3/:85 and snapshot.ts:162/:204 restore non-ignored changes during review; do not weaken this security guard for concurrency. The opt-in assumes suite outputs are gitignored and warns that other outputs can be removed. This story changes orchestration only, not permissions, credentials, sessions or guard internals.

Reporting and compatibility: packages/nax/src/workflow/run-summary.ts:98 builds the pure view from result.json, packages/nax/src/log-format/types.ts:82 declares it and packages/nax/src/log-format/workflow-summary.ts:36 renders it using formatDuration from formatter. Extend these files progressively in US-003, US-006, US-007 and US-009. Story record fields verdictMismatch/gateTimeouts/reviewOverlapMs and summary fields are optional; omit absent facts and zero overlap, rather than introducing empty arrays/undefined keys into persisted records or prior-summary equality assertions. Existing schemaVersion:1 at workflow/types.ts:105 needs no migration/bump; older results remain readable and are never rewritten. Positive overlap sums across stories only. Gate timeout summary strings use story IDs and gate lists. Mismatch rows are sorted by model; deferred counts reflect the record's current triage list and leave+newMinors keeps its old meaning.

Testing and execution plan: Reuse test/helpers/workflow-story-loop.ts:96 makeStoryLoopHarness scripting, makeStoryLoopAdvisor at :91, fixtures at :56, _workflowDeps and makeScriptedCallOp instead of mocking whole modules or reimplementing harnesses. Existing test/unit/workflow/story-loop-suite-first.test.ts:25 pins sequential phases and :48 pins the no-review-on-red-suite rule; keep these unchanged when opt-in is absent. Existing test/unit/workflow/stage-env.test.ts is 636 lines, so prefer focused new env integration files over pushing it past 800. Existing test/unit/operations/workflow-ops.test.ts:97 exercises review wiring and test/unit/workflow/gates.test.ts:53 covers exact result shape. Existing summary tests at test/unit/workflow/run-summary.test.ts:50 and test/unit/log-format/workflow-summary.test.ts are regression anchors for omitted fields. Unit-test pure selection/parser/timeout/end-state/formatting rules; integrate callOp retries and buildStoryEnv forwarding with fake agents and temporary files; test concurrency with controllable promises and a deterministic clock, never wall sleeps. New tests listed in expectedFiles are implementation deliverables, not standalone testing stories. Follow the nine-story binding order on one branch, allowing dependency-independent work only without conflicting edits; do not add dependencies. Run targeted Bun tests with explicit paths from packages/nax, and use existing package gates outside sandboxed pipeline execution; never bare bun test or bun run nax. Coverage is a separate outside-session CI concern, not an acceptance criterion. No package version bumps, dependency additions, root config edits or other workspace changes are needed.

Refine self-audit: All 166 numbered spec acceptance criteria were enumerated and checked in their original stories. The first 22/22/12/18/22/15/21/12/22 entries of US-001 through US-009 respectively remain the spec criteria in order; additional failure-table criteria follow those entries, never replace them. In particular the packagePrefix third argument (US-001.8), unchanged green scoped status after a resolver throw (US-001.15), findings-kept ledger suffixes (US-003.3-4), scoped-only configFacts call (US-005.18-19), stale-suite negative regression (US-005.20-21), no implementer between reruns (US-006.1), exactly one advisor question in total (US-006.3), omitted heading when no minors (US-007.16), existing minorsLeft meaning (US-007.20), real env options forwarding (US-008.12), sequential fallback and both settlement barriers (US-009.2/13-16), and formatDuration value (US-009.22) are retained. Corrected US-006.11 to explicitly retain status GATE_TIMEOUT from its original shared precondition.
